title: Tallifority Legit or Scam? 2026 Review: What to Check
description: Is Tallifority legit or a scam? We check its RM 1,022 minimum, its user-rating claims and the Malaysia-only sign-up limit on its own site.
author: Sophia Reynolds
excerpt: Is Tallifority legit or a scam? We check its RM 1,022 minimum, its user-rating claims and the Malaysia-only sign-up limit on its own site.
content:
Tallifority describes itself as an AI-driven trading platform for users in Malaysia who rely on automated strategies, real-time market insights and security features. Its site says registration is limited to verified residents of Malaysia, and it lists a minimum deposit of 1,022 RM.

Searches for Tallifority usually ask one thing: is it legit or a scam? The site answers that question itself, so this review sets out what it says and what it leaves open.

This review uses only what tallifority.com says about Tallifority. Claims the site makes without a source are attributed to it, and we say so where we could not check them.

Tallifority Explained: What the Site Describes

According to its site, Tallifority combines an AI engine with live market analysis to identify and act on trading opportunities. Users can switch between automated and manual trading, and the site describes a dashboard showing trades, performance data and signals.

The site also says it keeps 95% of funds in cold storage and uses 2FA and 256-bit SSL encryption. It does not name the company that operates the platform.

Tallifority: Where the Site Stands Up, Where It Doesn’t

Here is what the site offers, and what it does not back up.

What Tallifority states about itself:

  • A stated minimum deposit of 1,022 RM and a clear list of funding methods.
  • The site says there are no hidden fees and no registration costs.
  • Two-factor authentication and 256-bit SSL are described as security measures.
  • A demo or manual mode is not mentioned, but manual trading is described as an option.
  • The site links to Terms of Use and a Risk Disclosure, and it warns about copycat domains.

Where Tallifority Falls Short:

  • No company name, regulator or licence is given, so the legitimacy claim cannot be checked from the site.
  • The site claims 4M+ registered users, 98+ countries and $500M+ in customer deposits, with no source for any figure.
  • Ratings disagree within the same site: a 4.8 score from 1,247 reviews in one section, and 4.7 from 247 ratings in the FAQ and summary.
  • Three testimonials end with the same sentence, and the page shows Malaysia-only registration beside a claim of 98+ countries.
  • The site says “Live reserve audits” but gives no auditor or report to check.

A polished page and quoted user numbers are not evidence. Judge Tallifority on what you can check yourself.

What Happens Behind Tallifority, According to Its Site

According to the site, the AI engine scans real-time market data, looks at liquidity and volatility, and can execute trades automatically based on its analysis. Automation can be adjusted, and users can switch to manual control.

The site describes performance tracking and analytics, but it does not show a sample dashboard or explain how signals are scored.

The site also says “while AI enhances the experience, the platform is built to keep you in control at all times”. It does not describe how that control works in practice.

Getting Set Up: The Steps the Site Describes

This is the sign-up route as the Tallifority site lays it out. We did not open an account to check it.

1. Register

The site asks for your first name, last name, email, phone number and country code. Registration is limited to verified residents of Malaysia.

2. Fund your account

The site lists major credit cards, bank transfers and PayPal, with a 1,022 RM minimum deposit.

3. Start trading

Set your automation level and risk preferences, or trade manually. The site does not say whether a demo account is available.

The site says registration is quick and free. Check the terms before you fund the account, and have identity documents ready.

What Tallifority Costs: What the Site Says and Leaves Out

The site says there are no hidden fees, no subscription fees and no registration costs. It gives a 1,022 RM minimum deposit, but no trading, spread or withdrawal fee schedule.

A site that says it is transparent about pricing should be able to show a fee schedule. This one does not, so the true cost is not clear from the site.

Before you deposit, check these in writing:

  • The spread or commission on each trade, and how it is set.
  • Withdrawal fees, the minimum withdrawal and how the 24-hour timing is counted.
  • Any currency conversion charge if your card or bank is not in ringgit.
  • Whether automated trading carries a charge, and how it is billed.

Treat the “0 hidden fees” line as a claim until a full fee schedule is published.

What Tallifority Offers

The site lists equities, forex, commodities, precious metals, CFDs and cryptocurrencies, and says Bitcoin, Ethereum, stocks and forex are covered by its AI scanning.

  • Cryptocurrencies, named on the site as Bitcoin and Ethereum.
  • Equities and forex, described as opportunities the AI scans.
  • Commodities, precious metals and CFDs, listed on the site.

The site does not give a complete list of instruments or say which can be traded from Malaysia. Check the list inside your account.

Is Tallifority Legit?

The site uses phrases like “trusted”, “transparent” and “secure”, and says “Yes. This is an AI-powered trading platform” in answer to whether it is legit. These are the site's own statements, not an independent assessment.

The site also addresses copycat versions of itself, saying a legal process is under way to take them down, and says the official domain is tallifority.com.

What we could and could not confirm from the site:

  • The company that operates the platform and where it is registered: not named.
  • Which regulator oversees it, and under which licence number: not named.
  • The 1,247 reviews and 4.8 rating, and the 247 ratings and 4.7 score: no source, and the two sets of figures disagree.
  • The “live reserve audits”: no auditor or report given.

Checks you can run yourself:

  • Search the company name and any licence number on the official financial services register of Malaysia, and of the country you live in.
  • Ask in writing for the legal entity name, its registration number and the auditor behind the reserve audits.
  • Compare the domain you typed with tallifority.com, since the site warns about copycat domains.
  • Search the name for independent scam reports and complaints, and read them with care.
  • Test a small withdrawal before you add more funds.

A site that says it is legit is not proof of legitimacy. This section is general information, not legal or financial advice.

Mistakes Worth Avoiding with Tallifority

Most losses on platforms like this come from the decisions people make after signing up. A few worth flagging:

Accepting the site's own “Yes, it is legit” answer.

The answer comes from the platform. Check the company on the register yourself.

Relying on the user-rating figures.

The site gives two different ratings and no source for either.

Depositing the full amount at once.

Start with the 1,022 RM minimum, then test a withdrawal.

Ignoring the copycat warning.

Only register through the domain you have checked yourself, not through a link in an advert or a message.

A Quick Checklist Before You Deposit

Run through this before you send any money.

  • The operator and its regulator found on the official register.
  • A full fee schedule for trading, spreads and withdrawals obtained in writing.
  • The reserve audit and its auditor confirmed.
  • A small withdrawal completed before you add more funds.
  • The domain checked against tallifority.com.
  • Claims of user numbers and ratings treated as marketing until sourced.
Explore Tallifority

Who Tallifority May Suit, and Who Should Look Elsewhere

Tallifority may suit someone in Malaysia who wants an automated, AI-assisted tool, will check the company details first, and accepts that the money could be lost.

It is a poor fit for anyone who needs a named regulator and licence, a full fee schedule, or a sourced track record before depositing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Tallifority legit or a scam?

We could not confirm it from the site. The site says it is legit, but it names no operator, regulator or licence, and its user figures disagree with each other.

Is Tallifority a scam?

We cannot say either way. Test a small withdrawal early, and register only through the domain you have checked yourself.

What is the Tallifority minimum deposit?

1,022 RM, according to the site's FAQ.

Is Tallifority available outside Malaysia?

The site says registration is limited to verified residents of Malaysia. It also claims 98+ countries, but does not list them.

Does Tallifority charge fees?

The site says there are no hidden fees, but it gives no fee schedule. Ask for one in writing.

How long does a Tallifority withdrawal take?

The site says most requests are completed within 24 hours, using the same method as the deposit.

Does Tallifority guarantee profits?

The site makes no explicit guarantee, but it presents its AI as delivering fast, precise trades. Trading carries a risk of losing capital.

Where We Land on Tallifority

The Tallifority site presents an AI trading tool with a 1,022 RM minimum, a Malaysia-only sign-up and claims of no hidden fees. It does not name the company, a regulator, a licence or an auditor, and its own user figures disagree.

If you still want to look further, check the company on the register, get the fee schedule in writing, and test a withdrawal before you add more funds.
